utterances.text: And we forced the meeting in May to happen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Janet Handel
utterances.text: We said the summer season is coming on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Janet Handel
utterances.text: These safety matters are too critical.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Janet Handel
utterances.text: So, you know, we asked the question about the vetting agency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Janet Handel
utterances.text: We have to look into that, you know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Janet Handel
utterances.text: And has anybody gotten back to us?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Janet Handel
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Janet Handel
utterances.text: And it is something that is on, you know, our to-do list is to schedule the next meeting with them, which maybe they'll be more responsive at this point.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Diane Park
utterances.text: The other thing is that...

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Miriam, did you have a comment?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Miriam Applebaum
utterances.text: Since I'm really bothered by the noise, and they're not supposed to even start flying till eight o'clock, and there's been occasions, usually the bad guys who don't care,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Miriam Applebaum
utterances.text: like 7.15 in the morning, and like when my husband was sick, trying to recuperate from something, he sleeps in beyond 7.15, but it wakes him up, it wakes up people who might be up all night long.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Miriam Applebaum
utterances.text: You know, it's just, they,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Miriam Applebaum
utterances.text: I just don't care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Miriam Applebaum
utterances.text: And, you know, I know Janet has sent, like, I've taken photographs of them being right beneath my apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Miriam Applebaum
utterances.text: Or, you know, at 7.15 in the morning, she sent it on to Donald at the Skyport.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Miriam Applebaum
utterances.text: And no response.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Miriam Applebaum
utterances.text: Is there a way to force them to follow some rules?

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: That is the focus of today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: So thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: And I wanted to commend our intrepid high school student and entrepreneur here, Mateo.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: If you can't measure it, you can't improve it.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: So thank you for your work to measure helicopter noise and for partnering with the Waterside Association to take your technology and apply it to seaplanes.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: And we're now going to move to the next panel.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

chapters.summary: Hooks says the area has LaGuardia, the Mets, a soccer stadium, museums, and 2,500 housing units; the 7 train is overtaxed; she asks EDC to study the existing dock near LaGuardia for ferry service.
chapters.title: Assemblywoman Hooks urges Willets Point ferry stop

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Assemblymember Hooks is joining us virtually.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: If you're able to testify right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Janet Handel
utterances.text: Hair muted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: Oh, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Janet Handel
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: Can you all hear me?

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: We can hear you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: Hi, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: Thank you so much for giving me the opportunity to testify on behalf of the ferry stop, an additional ferry stop at the Willis Point Flushing Bay Promenade.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: I just would like to say I am Assemblywoman Lorinda Huggs, and I do sit on the Committee for Transportation as well as Economic Development in the New York State Assembly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: I want to thank the ADC for their presentation today on their vision plan for the ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: I just want to put a lot of things into perspective why this site is such a viable site for a furry stop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: And that is, and I want to echo also my colleague, my city council colleague, Chanel Thomas-Henry, and ditto everything that she has said thus far.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: But this area, just to put in perspective, has the LaGuardia Airport, the New York Mets, the New York

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: City Football Club Soccer Stadium that's coming, GovBall, the Queens Museum, the USTA, Metropolitan Park that's coming, several 5K walks, the Unisphere,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: the Hermanos Vasquez Circus, the Hong Kong Dragon Ball Festival, the Hall of Science, the Queens Zoo, and the Louis Armstrong House Museum.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: Each entity has a minimum of 5K people to over 25,000 people per event per year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: Then on top of that, this area has now become a tourist destination boom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: On top of that,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: We have the Willis Point 2,500 residential units, and we also have two projects currently coming up of affordable housing projects.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: That's 537 units for one facility, and I forgot about the number of...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: The number of units for the other one, I can't really think of it in my head right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: But needless to say, there has always been a conversation in the community about having a ferry stop to help alleviate the 7 train.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: The 7 train is already like bursting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: out the seams with people and it's already overtaxed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: As you now have targeted the East Elmers community for development of large housing projects, you combine that with the fact that there seems to be historically a bad practice of putting the cart before the horse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: Development projects are being fast-tracked and infrastructure is being slow-walked.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: As we provide development, we have a fiscal responsibility and we must be prudent to build an infrastructure to sustain it before they are completed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: Now, I want to just say I know that there was some, he's not there, so he can't answer the question, but I know there has been some minor study as far as being able to dock closer to the promenade.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: But I don't think that there was a study, and I'm asking that there is a study.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: There's already a dock on the side of the Guadalquivir Airport for larger, heavier vessels.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: If that can be added to the vision study for the ferry stop as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: I think that would be a viable spot for it because it was already built to sustain that type of vessel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: So I just wanted to put my bid in to say, you know, please really, really look at this being a ferry stop for this area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larinda Hooks
utterances.text: Thank you all.

chapters.summary: The Disabled in Action vice president says ferries are hard to find; he urges an accessible bus stop at every landing, signage from the curb, and OMNY integration, citing Sydney and Vancouver.
chapters.title: Michael Ring calls for accessible bus stops and signage at ferry landings

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Assemblywoman.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Our next panel is going to be Monica Bartley from Disabled in Action, Jean Ryan,

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Kathleen Collins, Michael Ring, and Jabrel Jolo from the Flossie organization.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you for joining us.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: And thank you for waiting.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: It's a longer hearing than we expected.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin whenever you're ready.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Michael Ring.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I'm Vice President of Disabled in Action of Greater New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: If anyone needs a verbal description of my appearance, I'm a 63-year-old white guy wearing a hat that says Disabled in Action and a hoodie that says I ran a marathon because I'm complex.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: And I wanted to talk about the ferries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I really like the ferries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I enjoy taking the ferry whenever I can.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: My children have half a dozen friends that work on the ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: But if you're disabled, it's hard to find the ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: And I would urge the city to add an accessorized bus stop at every ferry landing so that accessorized knows where to go.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: And like the curb cut effect, that curb cuts help everyone, if every ferry landing, ferry stop had an accessorized bus stop, that would mean it would have an address that's a drop-off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: It would be an easy place to find if you want to get to the ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: And I often am near the Pier 6 ferry in Brooklyn Bridge Park.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: There's no signage that tells you how to get to it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: to the ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: So if there would be accessible signage, how to get from the curb to the ferry, it would just be a very helpful thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: More people would be using the ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: And one other thing I wanted to add, this summer I happened to travel a lot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I was in cities that had great ferry systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: Sydney and Vancouver, people use the ferry a lot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: It's one payment system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: You know, it would be very complicated, but the city's good at doing big, complicated things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: If the OmniCard would work on the ferry, more people would use the ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: It would, you know, make it a transfer or maybe a slight additional fare.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: You guys do the math.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: I would encourage that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Ring
utterances.text: And I'm running out of time, so I'll...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Janet Handel
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: The Disabled in Action treasurer says the disability community must be consulted before decisions; Local Law 68 requires four-point securement; she calls for accessible kiosks, audio, and visual announcements.
chapters.title: Kathleen Collins demands disability consultation and four-point securement

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Good afternoon, my name is Kathleen Collins and I'm the treasurer of Disabled in Action right now, but next month I will just be a member of Disabled in Action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: I'm going to be in the background.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: First of all, all public and private transportation, including future ferry,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Party boats and seaplane service must be accessible to the entire disability community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: And I give you applause over there, Councilwoman, for various, I'm sorry if I'm misstating your name.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Thank you for asking that question of the,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Economic Development Corporation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: I really, really do appreciate that from my

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Today I'm going to focus on the New York City Ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: The disability community must be consulted before decisions are made and not after problems arise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: We are the experts on our own access needs, yet too often we are treated as an afterthought.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Wheelchair users need four-point securement to travel safely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: New York City Ferry must provide and maintain this equipment, keep wheelchair spaces clear, and train staff to assist passengers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Local Law 68 requires four-point securement and inadequate restraints put lives at risk, not only our lives, but other passengers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Blind and low vision passengers need accessible ticket kiosks, functioning audio features, and clear wayfinding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Deaf and hard of hearing passengers need visual announcements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: All passengers need safe, accessible routes to and from ferry landings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: New York City Ferry must also provide an accessible digital way to apply for disability fare discounts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: We urge New York City EDC to establish a formal ongoing consultation process with the broad cross-section of the disability community,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: develop an accessibility plan with specific deadlines and accountability, and involve disabled New Yorkers in designing and evaluating these future ferry stops that you are considering today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: And to consider technology.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Equal access to transportation is a civil right, not a courtesy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Accessibility must be built in from the beginning, not

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: added to the fact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Nothing about us without us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathleen Collins
utterances.text: And I'll be submitting a long testimony later and the short one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Janet Handel
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Bartley says wheelchair spaces are occupied by sightseers and there is no four-point securement; brakes are insufficient; she urges clear spaces, staff training, secure ramps, and City Island ferry service.
chapters.title: Monica Bartley describes wheelchair safety problems on NYC Ferry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: Good afternoon, chairs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: My name is Monica Bartley and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: My name is Monica Bartley, and I'm a member of Disabled in Action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: I want to express my serious concerns about wheelchair safety on New York City Ferry and urge the city to take action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: On a recent trip to Governor's Island, I couldn't access the designated wheelchair space because parents and children were occupying it to sightsee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: I was left in the middle of the ferry, worried that my wheelchair would move if the boat suddenly rocked or jolted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: At times, I've had to position my chair behind a seat just so I could hold on for safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: No wheelchair user should have to travel in fare.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: I urge NYC Ferry to install four-point wheelchair securement on all ferries as required by Local Law 68 of 2005.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: Ferries naturally roll and sway, and wheelchair brakes alone are not enough to keep a chair in place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: Without proper securement, wheelchairs can slide, tip, or break loose, putting wheelchair users and other passengers at risk of serious injury.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: Four-point securement provides greater safety and backup if one of the attachments fails.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: NYC Ferry must also keep designated wheelchair spaces clear of tables, strollers, and other obstructions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: Deck staff should ensure these spaces remain accessible during boarding and throughout the trip.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: Staff must also be trained to proactively offer assistance, guide wheelchair users to the securement area, and help secure their chairs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: Finally, all securement equipment must be regularly inspected and promptly repaired or replaced when it is

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: corroded, stuck, or not working properly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: Some, finally, some ferry docking ramps also raise safety concerns.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: At certain terminals, passengers who use wheelchairs have experienced ramps rocking and swaying during boarding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: These ramps must be secured more firmly to reduce

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: reduce the risk to passengers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: And finally, my third panel, support extending the ferry service to City Island, a place I frequently visit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: The Disabled in Action president says the 2005 law required four-point securement, but Hornblower ferries have only two-point and workers never secure wheelchairs; nothing changed after meetings.
chapters.title: Jean Ryan says NYC Ferry has regressed on wheelchair securement

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Hi, I'm Jean Ryan, President of Disabled in Action of Metropolitan New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: I use a wheelchair and I ride NYC ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: In 2005, DIA got the City Council to pass the Trailblazing Accessible Ferry Bill that required all NYC

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: commuter ferries to be wheelchair accessible because the ADA did not cover commuter ferries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: At that time, there were few commuter ferries in New York City, and the ones that were here had steps and steep ramps to get to them,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: while the boats had upright boards across the bottom of the doorways and bathrooms with doorways that were above the floor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: We couldn't get into the cabin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: The law required two dedicated wheelchair spaces with a four-point securement in the front of the ferries, and we had that with the previous vendor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: We also worked with them to design and test safe docks and piers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Once Hornblower took over the contract, the ferries only had a two-point securement, which is not safe, and the workers never secure us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: There is no specific...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: space for wheelchairs on the ferries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: On one trip with many senior citizens on the ferry, I had to ask people in front and in back of me to move because if the ferry jerked, my wheelchair could move and badly injure their legs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: I met with Hornblower, DOT, and EDC in a virtual meeting about safety and the wheelchair requirements on NYC ferries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Nothing changed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Over the years, I testified before this city council about ferry safety, and nothing changed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: We met with EDC about ferry safety for wheelchair users and people who are blind, and it seems that they have no will to follow the law or provide safe conditions for people with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Safety and following the law are not optional.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

chapters.summary: The Flossie Organization founder says Canarsie's waterfront has unrealized potential; two mayoral administrations failed to deliver; he urges passage of Intro 704 to revitalize the pier and reconnect families.
chapters.title: Jabril Jallo supports Canarsie Pier ferry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Maloney and Council Members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: My name is Jabril Jallo, and I'm the founder and executive director of the Flossie Organization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: And I am here today in strong support of Intro 704, introduced by Council Member Mercedes Narcisse, to establish a ferry at Canarsie Pier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: For Canarsie, this is much more than transportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: It's about reclaiming our waterfront.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: Expanding recreational opportunities for working families, and ensuring our community receives its fair share of public investment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: Canarsie sits along the beautiful shores of the Jamaica Bay with one of Brooklyn's most extraordinary waterfront assets right in our backyard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: Yet for decades, we have failed to realize the full recreational, economic, and community potential for our beautiful pier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: Historically, Canarsie was a vibrant waterfront destination where families gathered to enjoy boating and ferry connections along the Jamaica Bay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: The waterfront was a place where neighbors gathered and children played, and generations of families created lasting memories.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: Today, much of that vibrancy has disappeared.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: A waterfront should be much more than a beautiful view.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: It should be a place where families can spend an afternoon, children can explore, seniors can gather, and neighbors can connect with one another.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: Two consecutive mayoral administrations recognize the need for ferry service in Canarsie.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: acknowledge the importance of connecting our community, and ultimately both failed to deliver.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: Today, we urge the council to advance and pass Intro 704 and make a clear legislative commitment to establishing regular public ferry service to the Canarsie Pier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: Let this hearing mark the beginning of a new chapter for Canarsie, one defined by, not by unfulfilled promises, but by progress.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: Establish the ferry, revitalize the pier, reconnect our families to the waterfront.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: Thank you so much for the opportunity to testify and your consideration of Intro 704.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: I want to thank you all for your testimony and thank you to Disability in Action in particular for your advocacy and highlighting some of the concerns that will need to be addressed by EDC and in the next RFP.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Any questions from the council members?

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: The Brooklyn Center for Independence of the Disabled advocate says boarding is only part of an accessible trip; she urges four-point securement, staff training, step-free routes, and accessible ticket machines.
chapters.title: Elizabeth Valdez calls for four-point securement and accessible landings

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: The next panel is Henry.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Smith from Long Island City Partnership, Lauren Nye, Roxanne Delgard, Elizabeth Valdez.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: And I'm going to call up a few more names.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: John Doyle.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Carolyn Schroeder, Kim Woodruff, Michael Shane Lee, and Dan Treber.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Is it too many people?

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: We might need one more chair.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: And whoever is ready to begin may begin.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: You may begin whenever you're feeling ready.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Good afternoon, my name is Elizabeth Valdez and I am the systems advocate at the Brooklyn Center for Independence of the Disabled and a wheelchair user.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Today I am calling for two essential improvements, proper four-point wheelchair securement on ferry vessels and full accessibility at every new ferry landing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: For wheelchair users, being able to board a ferry is only one part of an accessible trip.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: We must also be able to travel safely once we are on board.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: I urge New York City Ferry to install four-point securement systems designed for use on its vessels with adequate space for different wheelchair sizes, including power wheelchairs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Staff must be trained to use these systems correctly, inspect the equipment, and assist riders respectfully.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: We should not have to spend the trip worrying about our wheelchairs shifting as the vessel moves or docks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Our safety deserves the same attention as everyone else's.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: As New York City Ferry develops new station and landings, accessibility must be included from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: That means a continuous step-free route from the surrounding sidewalk to the vessel, accessible curb ramps, wide pathways, and boarding ramps that remain usable as tides change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: It also means accessible ticket machines, clear signs in both audible and visual service announcements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: must serve people with mobility, vision, hearing, and other disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: The city should involve people with disabilities in reviewing designs, in testing new landings before they open and establish a clear process for reporting and fixing barriers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: New York City Ferry connects people to jobs, medical appointments, family,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: and community life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: People with disabilities deserve to make those connections with safety, dignity, and independence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your testimony.

chapters.summary: A 31-year City Island resident says the main street has shuttered shops and little foot traffic; he feels unconnected and says a ferry would help retirees and families visit other boroughs.
chapters.title: Michael Shanley says City Island needs ferry investment

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: Hello, my name is Michael Shanley.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: I am a lifelong Bronx resident and have lived on City Island for the past 31 years with my wife and family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: I am in full support of a ferry landing on City Island for many, many reasons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: When I first discovered City Island years ago and considered it as a potential place to buy a home and raise my family, I always said that our beautiful little island had so much potential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: Unfortunately, over the past 31 years, we've never reached it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: City Island Avenue today, unfortunately, and I hate to say, looks like a depressed has-been of a town.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: There are so many shuttered shop fronts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: The businesses that are opening are really struggling just to keep their doors open.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: There's very little foot traffic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: My wife and I are recent retirees, and our plan is to spend our retired years exploring our beautiful city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we feel so unconnected to the rest of New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: In fact, City Island is often even left off maps of New York City because we don't have a direct subway line.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: We feel like we're the forgotten borough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: We need the investment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: We need access.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: My oldest son and his wife live in Astoria.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: You know, it's so convenient for us to take the ferry, transfer at 98th Street, and go to Astoria, Queens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: The same, we like to visit other boroughs, Brooklyn and Queens and Staten Island, but it just is so much more complicated not having transportation options.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Shanley
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: A City Island mom and ice cream shop owner says a ferry would expand high school options, reduce commutes, and bring foot traffic; she addresses parking and cost concerns and wants Main Street thriving.
chapters.title: Kim Woodruff says City Island ferry would help families and businesses

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: My name is Kim Woodruff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: I am a City Island resident of 14 years, a mom, and a new City Island business owner.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Can you make sure to turn on your microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: My name is Kim Woodruff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: I am a City Island resident of 14 years, a mom, and a new City Island business owner.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: I wholeheartedly support bringing a ferry stop to City Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: As a mom, I know firsthand how much a ferry would open up opportunities for families like mine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: For example, it would expand the pool of high schools that City Island kids could realistically attend.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: My daughter was accepted into one of the most desirable high schools in the city, but she has an hour and a half commute each way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: Even the very closest high schools require students to travel at least 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: Transportation is a real limitation for families on the island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: As a business owner on City Island, I meet people every day who love visiting the island, but complain about how difficult it is to get here, especially without a car.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: Many say they would come back more often if it were easier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: When I mention the possibility of a ferry, they're thrilled.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: I have no doubt people would use it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: From my shop, I see so many empty storefronts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: I'd love to see our Main Street thriving again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: At my ice cream shop, I've been able to provide jobs for local teenagers who are earning their own money, developing skills, and contributing to our community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: We need more opportunities like that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: A ferry could bring foot traffic, support existing businesses, and encourage new ones to open.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: I also want to address concerns about parking and cost.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: Why would people drive to City Island to catch a ferry when they have transportation options closer to home?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: On weekends, a ferry could actually reduce traffic by bringing visitors here without their cars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: And while ferries cost money to operate, we should also consider the economic benefits of increased business activity, jobs, and sales tax revenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: Finally, a ferry would improve our quality of life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: The idea of simply walking down to a ferry and going somewhere in the city without worrying about traffic, parking, or multiple transfers is a dream.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: City Island is a special place with so much potential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: A ferry would connect us to the rest of New York City, create opportunities for our children, support local businesses, and help revitalize our main street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: Got it right in time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Woodruff
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: A fourth-generation resident says City Island has one bridge and the nearest subway is three miles away; she asks the study to count visitors, Heart Island families, and new residents, and to diversify the fleet.
chapters.title: Lauren Nye presents research supporting City Island ferry study

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Maloney and council members of the committees, especially CM Ferrejas, who has helped to shepherd Intro 1032.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: My name is Lauren Nye.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: I'm a fourth generation City Island resident, a homeowner.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: I've studied extensively New York City's ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: I have an MPA capstone from CUNY Baruch analyzing the special City Island District.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: I work at the Association for Neighborhood and Housing Development, but today I'm here as a resident in support of Intro 1032.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: City Island has one bridge and the nearest subway is three miles away through the city's largest park.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: For at least the last decade, our main street has had consistently over 20 vacant storefronts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: From 2010 to 2020, the city grew by 600,000 people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: City Island's population is stagnant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: Without proper transit, it cannot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: In 2019, EDC concluded that ridership to City Island was low.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: However, it missed key riders, day visitors to our restaurants, small businesses, Orchard Beach, families visiting Heart Island, now under parks where New York City

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: has many residents who have been lost to COVID, and new residents who would be able to move to City Island because transit would allow it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: The Rockaway route was also once written off for low ridership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: Today is one of the system's busiest, and the Rockaway Rocket further highlights demand to the Rockaways for leisure and tourism.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: That is exactly the kind of opportunity City Island presents, and without the good data and planning, we miss this opportunity once again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: Based on my research, I request that Intro 1032 study five things, counting the full ridership, model visitors, Heart Island families, and new residents, not just commuters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: Economic development potentials, which has also been brought up today, is another part of the study.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: Diversify the fleet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: New York City Ferry started with 150 passenger boats only and ordered new ones based on busier routes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: A smaller vessel would make scissor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: Smaller routes, more accessible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: Assess the City Island boatyard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: We haven't talked at all about the fact that the second repair yard is in Connecticut right now, and City Island is a special purpose district with a nautical purpose.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: Connected to housing, City of Yes calls for more housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: Our district built 10 units, or 26 units, from 2014 to 2020, while neighboring Bronx districts built more than 1,000.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: My commute to Fidei is 90 minutes each way, but I'm not here for that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lauren Nye
utterances.text: I'm here because we have a chance to impact transit, economic, and housing equity, and I hope this study can help ensure that opportunity, and I'll submit written testimony with more full research and data that I have collected over my 10 years studying this matter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: A vintage toy store owner says his Williamsburg flea market thrived when the ferry arrived; he used proceeds to buy a City Island building and says his son's commute would improve.
chapters.title: Dan Treiber says ferry would boost City Island businesses

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: My name is Dan Treiber.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: I run a vintage toy store on City Island Avenue called Dan's Parents House for the past 10 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: Previous to running Dan's Parents House, it was Trader John's, a nautical junk shop for 50 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: We are housed in an 1860s building that we purchased and saved from demolition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: Previous to our storefront, I did the Brooklyn flea market for 16 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: Arguably our most successful year was in Williamsburg when they introduced the ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: I consistently watched people get off the money, I mean, sorry, get off the ferry, walk into the market, and spend hard-earned money.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: This not only impacted the people in the community, but the small businesses that were at that market every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: We took that money and we purchased 239 City Island Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: Without the ferry, I wouldn't be at that store today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: We've consistently seen, you know, vacant storefronts come and go, but City Island is sort of, I...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: Because from my perspective, I see it on the upswing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: We have a new owner of Lickety Split, which is the local ice cream shop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: We have a successful coffee bar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: And I think that if we had the ferry, there would be more people getting out and walking and spending money and exploring our wonderful town.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: In addition to running the vintage store, more importantly, I have two children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: I have 15.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: year old twins in the New York City high school system, one of which goes to Manhattan Center for Science and Math.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: He has to get up at six to take the 705 bus, which is inconsistent at best, to take the sixth train to 116th Street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: If he could walk to the ferry and take it there, not only would he be a happier child, but he'd be more likely to be helpful in the future.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: So as a parent and a local store owner, I feel like a ferry directly to City Island would be very beneficial.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dan Treiber
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: The City Island Rising petition has over 2,500 signatures; 43% of residents commute over an hour; EDC's 2018 study projected a 40% commute reduction; he asks the council to pass Intro 1032.
chapters.title: John Doyle presents petition for City Island ferry

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Maloney.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Fedeas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: And thank you to all the supporters of Intro 1032.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: Five years ago, after extensive discussions and at the suggestion of then-Senator Biagi, City on Rising started a Change.org petition to support ferry service to City Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: To even our surprise, the petition took off and now sits at over 2,500 signatures, more than double any other proposal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: And I also have a few hundred in hand, which I will submit before the closing of the period here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: This quickly snowballed into extensive outreach, op-eds, media coverage, debates, and discussions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: We launched YesCityIslandFerry.com in 2023, pushing policymakers and advocacy groups like the Waterfront Alliance to work with us to make this happen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: In 2024, community members met with then-Councilmember Marmorado and then-Economic Development Chair Committee Chair Amanda Fedeas to discuss bringing a ferry to City Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: In the last two years, we have lobbied and secured the support from elected officials, State Senator Natalia Fernandez, Assemblymember Benedetto, who you heard from earlier, and our current Councilmember, Councilmember Aldebar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: So to anyone listening or watching at home, saying this bill came out of nowhere ignores the many hours community members have put into this campaign, the many documented efforts to get us to where we are today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: In only two weeks, we were able to get 350 signatures to support new legislation, and as you can see, the overwhelming majority are from City Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: So first, I just want to say as a longtime City Island resident,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: 35 years this August.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: I'm fortunate to work nearby.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: But the overwhelming amount of city islanders aren't so fortunate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: In fact, according to the census, 43% of city islanders spent over an hour traveling for work, and that's only one way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: We're talking about spending 10% of your day, or even more of your waking hours, commuting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: According to the EDC's own 2018 study, residents would see their commute times drop by 40%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: I encourage you to read the stories that have been submitted and to talk about how dramatically improving the lives of our neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: I think we should center them in the discussions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: And I would just further just point out that there has been, you know, there have been 20 speaking storefronts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: We have a video.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: We'll submit to the evidence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: But this has been going on for over 20 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: It's time to try something new.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Doyle
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Members.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: I want to thank Elizabeth Valdez for your holistic description of what accessibility on our near city ferry systems means.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: And thank you to the advocates for City Island.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: We've got our change.org petition here.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: More signatures than we can count.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Any questions from the...

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: And I'm excited to take the ferry to City Island someday.

chapters.summary: A resident says the ferry subsidy is high, City Island's median income is over $100,000, and density is low; a previous study found only 225 commuters; she suggests Orchard Beach instead.
chapters.title: Roxanne Delgado opposes City Island ferry as inequitable

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: There was one final testimony, Roxanne Delgado, and I think that is the last person to testify.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: In person, then we have some online testimony.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: We'll be moving.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: On Zoom to Catherine Sebeck next, but first Roxanne.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: Thank you, committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: I'd like to say that my name is Roxanne Delgado.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: I'm a resident council district 13, which includes City Island in the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: I do not support intro 1032.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: I question whether socializing City Island Ferry is financially responsible or fair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: In 2025, New York City Ferry required over

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: required over $8 operating subsidies for every ride.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: A controller report found that earlier calculation of its significant costs did not include depreciation, and now the fares has recently increased from yesterday to $5.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: A rider survey conducted by NYCED states that the median household income that it serves is over 100,000, which is similar to City Island's median household income.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: And this population is extremely low density and is the furthest distance from which it requires more subsidies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: And who will pay for it?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: The riders or the taxpayers?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: A previous feasibility study identified only 225 city islanders will commute to Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: This raises serious concerns about if demand meets this pet project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: If the city council decides to do another study, why not Orchard Beach?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: The city invests over $114 million to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: recreate the pavilion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: The Orchard Beach is the only public beach in the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: And last year only generated a million dollars for the city funds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: Most of it was from parking fees, barely 200,000 concession fees.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: Based on the large capital investment in Orchard Beach, why not have the ferry at Orchard Beach to help the economic development in that pavilion that cost us over $100 million?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: Not to mention this year, per vendor, they did not do fare well in this year's pavilion, but it is the first year, but let's hope it could help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: Increase Orchard Beach and the parks revenue, the city general funds money.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: And I would like to say though that we have to think about equity because before we invest in, well, it's about equity, that's what I'm here for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: I think subsidizing a pet project for a group that's politically connected, as you can see, that has high income at the cost of the rest of the Bronx is not fair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: I thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Roxanne Delgado
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

chapters.summary: Sebeck says the testimony portal shows more opposition than eight; a previous council member survey found residents did not want a ferry; she asks the bill to specify Orchard Beach and agrees with EDC's concerns.
chapters.title: Kathy Sebeck says City Island Civic Association opposes ferry location

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: And next on Zoom, first Kathy Sebeck, followed by Dan McSweeney.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Yes, we can hear you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Oh, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: I was on the phone and the Zoom here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: We submitted, my name is Kathy Seaback.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: I'm from the City Island Civic Association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: We submitted our testimony along with many members of our community to the portal for a hearing and also to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: At council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: NYC, council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: I hope you look at all of that because I don't think Councilman Farias is eight opposed and 354 is an accurate portrayal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: That may be the email she received, but the public is not asked to send the email to her.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: So I would hope you please consider the testimony in those two places.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: We also sent to her and to the over 1,700 signatures on petitions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Our civic association has hundreds of members, and I hope you consider that before you move forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: The rollout of this bill, yes, ferry has been discussed quite a bit on City Hall for years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Councilman Marmorato was not in support of a ferry here and did a survey and found the residents did not want it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: And we requested Orchard Beach to be in the study.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Now, the parsing of words of it's adjacent, I think before they go forward with this bill, they should amend it to say Orchard Beach or is adjacent mean all of Palin Bay Park.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: I think it would be clear to the community and the public if we knew this, because it was very confusing to a lot of the residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Not that they didn't understand, but what does adjacent mean?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: And I think a clear form of that would be fine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: But you could read the testimony sitting on small.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: I appreciate Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Wong because.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Almost everything Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Wong said is part of our argument as some of the residents from City Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: I agree with what he said, and I'm glad a person that is an expert on this, that we are a pretty informed association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: I don't think traffic will be relieved by a ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Maybe when at Orchard Beach, the cars on the road would not come to Orchard Beach and take a ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: But this has been an argument ongoing, and it was just rolled out on Friday by Councilman Abador.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: To let the community know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: And also, Amanda Farias was an email to me on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: That's not a lot of time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: The community supports our effort.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kathy Sebeck
utterances.text: Thank you so much for listening.

chapters.summary: The Manhattan Community Board 6 district manager says seaplanes mostly fly between Manhattan and the Hamptons; residents get noise, risk, and pollution; CB6 has passed resolutions for 30 years and supports Intro 1115.
chapters.title: Jesus Perez says East River residents bear seaplane risk

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Next is Dan McSweeney.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: If you're on the Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monica Bartley
utterances.text: Not present.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Next is Jesus Perez.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jean Ryan
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Maloney and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: My name is Jesus Perez and I am the District Manager of Manhattan Community Board 6.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: Our district runs along the East River from 14th to 59th Street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: As you've already heard, our district knows firsthand the annoyances and dangers of the many seaplanes that travel up and down the East River.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: The panel of waterside residents you heard earlier more eloquently articulated the conditions and violations on the East River better than I could, so I will not repeat them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: But I will say that the people of our district bear nearly all of the risk of these flights, and they get almost none of the benefit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: Seaplanes take off and land near thousands of homes closer than regulations allow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: These seaplanes are mostly flying between Manhattan and the Hamptons, and that is a convenience for the few rather than the many, and it is paid for in noise, risk, and pollution by everyone else.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: As Councilmember Maloney mentioned during her questioning, Manhattan Community Board 6 has passed resolutions going back 30 years that the Skyport site should serve the community rather than the few.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: Instead, EDC came back to us last year with a $12 million rehabilitation project that included a larger seaplane dock, all for a facility that brings in a fraction of that and upsets its neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: It's not on the agenda today, but we thank Chair Maloney for introducing Intro 1115.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: that would facilitate the monitoring of noise levels around seaplane bases.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: Residents deserve hard numbers on the noise they live with every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: And we urge all other council members to sign on as co-sponsors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: But measuring the problem is only the first step.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: We need to remember that the East River belongs to New Yorkers, not to the seaplanes for the few of them who can afford them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesus Perez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your testimony.

chapters.summary: A City Island resident supports studying ferry service but suggests Orchard Beach; she describes months of 311 complaints about loud music from party boats until 2-4 AM and asks for proactive enforcement.
chapters.title: Katie McCormick describes late-night party boat noise

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Next is Katie McCormick, followed by Kiana Diaz.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jabril Jallo
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: Good afternoon, and thank you for allowing me to speak today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: My name is Katie McCormick, and I am a City Island resident.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: I support the city's efforts to study ferry service to City Island, but I believe Orchard Beach should seriously be considered as a location for a ferry landing, given its parking, open space, accessibility, and existing waterfront infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: But I also want to address another issue that is directly affecting waterfront residents, the ongoing problem of late-night party boat noise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: The issue of party boats, illegal charters, and nighttime activity on New York City's waterways is not theoretical for those of us who live along the waterfront.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: For years, residents around City Island and the surrounding waterways have been dealing with extremely loud, amplified music coming from boats late at night and at times into the early morning hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: personally spent

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: I've personally spent months reporting these incidents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: I have submitted 311 complaints, provided videos, contacted the NYPD and Harbor Patrol, and communicated repeatedly with elected officials.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: There have been nights when the music continued for hours, despite repeated calls for assistance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: Behind every one of these complaints are real people who are trying to live their lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: We have families, working parents, and small children who need a good night's sleep.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: When loud music continues until 2, 3, or 4 in the morning, it doesn't just disturb us in the moment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: It affects our children's sleep, our ability to function at work, and our entire family's well-being the following day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: No family should have to wonder whether we will be able to sleep in their own home because of loud music coming from boats on the water.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: I appreciate the officers and the Harbor Patrol personnel who have responded, and I recognize that they are working within their resources and procedures available to them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: My concern is the larger system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: Too often, enforcement feels reactive rather than preventative.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: By the time a resident identifies where the music is coming from, makes a complaint, and waits for someone to respond, the activity may have already been going on for hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: And when a complaint is closed, that does not necessarily mean the underlying problem has been resolved.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: What waterfront communities need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: Sorry, is consistent predictable enforcement present during the hours when these problems actually occur?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: If the city knows that certain waterways become hotspots on certain nights and during certain hours, resources should be positioned there proactively.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: rather than relying on residents to call after the problem has already begun.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: I would ask the council to go beyond the number of summonses issued or complaints closed and ask more important questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: Are waterfront residents actually experiencing a sustained improvement in their quality of life?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Katie.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

chapters.summary: The Manhattan CB12 district manager says the Inwood rezoning adds 4,000 homes and only the 1 and A trains serve the area; she asks the city to assess Dyckman Street infrastructure and explore routes.
chapters.title: Kiana Diaz urges ferry service for Inwood and Washington Heights

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Next up is Kiana Diaz, followed by Lillian Krieg.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: And we please ask if people can stay within the time limit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: Hi, good morning, Chair Maloney, Majority Leader Abreu, and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: My name is Kiana Diaz.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: I am the District Manager of Manhattan Community Board 12, representing the communities of Washington Heights and Inwood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: I'm here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: It is not on the agenda, but I would like for, our board would like for our comments to be on the record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: In regards to Councilmember Carmen de la Rosa's bill, Intro 163, that's 2026, expanding ferry services to Upper Manhattan, specifically Inwood, at La Marina and 10th Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: Our communities are experiencing significant growth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: Through the Inwood rezoning, there are nearly 4,000 new homes that will be built in Inwood, specifically along 9th Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
