utterances.text: Yet our transportation infrastructure remains heavily dependent on two subway lines, the 1 and the A line, both running along the west side of Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: For residents that travel to the east side, this can add to 20 to 30 minutes of their commute.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: As our population grows, we risk overcrowding an already strained subway system, where overcrowding can lead the commuters waiting for multiple trains just to board.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: We must explore alternative transportation options before our existing infrastructure becomes even more overwhelmed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: We recognize EDC's concerns about projected ridership on the Hudson River and height restrictions posed by bridges over the Harlem River.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: However, these challenges should prompt us to explore solutions, not rule out our communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: Dyckman Street already has waterfront infrastructure that could provide a starting point for evaluating ferry services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: We are asking the city to seriously assess the existing infrastructure, explore viable routes, and engage our community before concluding that there is insufficient demand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: Our residents are actually very excited about the possibility of ferry service uptown.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: In fact, at one of our local high schools, Washington High School, the students have developed their own proposed ferry routes connecting Upper Manhattan to parts of the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: Ridership projections must account for more than comparisons with existing subway travel times.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: They must consider our district's growing population, the need for better connections to destinations across the city, and the potential to reduce traffic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: Our communities attract visitors from across the city, including members of the Dominican diaspora, who return to access local business.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Your time expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: May I finish quickly?

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: You can finish with one line.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: Lastly, we just ask that expansion must be guided by equity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: We're hoping for a standardized citywide fare.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: And the commitment to expand the ferry services to new areas will not come at the expense of continued investment in underserved communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: A City Island resident says the bill requires a study then construction within a year; she asks about traffic, parking, flooding, zoning, boaters, and oyster restoration, and wants full transparency and amendments.
chapters.title: Lillian Krieg asks for community engagement and environmental review

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: I'd now like to call on Lillian Craig.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: by Neve Wallace and Ricardo Garcia.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Maloney and council members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: My name is Lillian Krieg, a longtime City Island resident and homeowner.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: I speak for an active community that votes in every election and on every level.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: First, involving our community at every step.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: City Island has one bridge, flood-prone streets, and a special district created in 1977 to protect our nautical character.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: Intro 1032 requires a study, then construction of a landing within a year if a site is found.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: I see the report posted online, but no required hearing on City Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: EDC's 2025 Fairies Report promises community engagement for the vision, which was due this fall, but apparently it's going to be in the summer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: Has that begun for City Island, and how does that relate to this bill?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: What is the community engagement like?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: Second, what the study leaves out, EDC's own report says that City Island remoteness, low population, and limited public waterfront require thoughtful assessment, and limited parking is a key concern.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: Yet, Intro 1032 does not list traffic, parking, flooding, housing, or zoning pressure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: In Astoria, a developer told New York Times in 2017 his firm bought as many properties as it could the moment the ferry was announced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: We ask that the bill be amended.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: Third, our boating and environmental communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: Boaters have docked for generations, supported by boatyards, marinas, and yacht clubs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: And neighbors and students are restoring oysters in our waters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: report notes other harbor operators' concerns kept a Manhattan landing from being built.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: What is being done to consult city and boaters, marinas, yacht clubs, and oyster reef and environmental scientists, formally in public and at each stage?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: Fourth, the environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: EDC's description of the vision lists zero emission vessels, but not wakes, underwater noise, wildlife, or environmental review.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: Research shows that wakes, noise, and dredging can affect shorelines and shellfish.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: EDC says landings are limited by water depth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: What is City Islands and what dredging would be needed?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: At Coney Island, EDC reports shifting required continual dredging, and CBS reported that a $70,000 state fine and landing costing over $12.5 million was built and removed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: What will be different here?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: We will be involved at every step, and we ask for full transparency every study, permit, application, and record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: We vote, and we will remember who listened.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: The feasibility study should not be a pipeline to construction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lillian Krieg
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: The NYCFC communications manager says Etihad Park opens next year and Gotham FC will play there in 2028; ferry service would give fans an alternative to driving and reduce congestion.
chapters.title: Neve Wallace of NYCFC supports Willets Point ferry

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Next, we have Nev Wallace, followed by Ricardo Garcia.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kiana Diaz
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Maloney, Chair Abreu, and committee members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: My name is Neve Wallace, and I serve as manager of communications at New York City Football Club.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: I am delivering this testimony on behalf of Brad Sims, the chief executive officer of New York City Football Club.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: The club thanks you for the opportunity to submit testimony in support of Intro 846, legislation that would establish regular public ferry service connecting Willits Point and with Midtown and the Financial District.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: The club thanks Councilmember Chanel Thomas-Henry and all of the bill co-sponsors for their commitment to expanding transportation access and connectivity across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: New York City FC is proud to be building Etihad Park in Willits Point.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: Once built, it will be New York City's first ever soccer-specific stadium.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: In less than a year, Etihad Park will open its doors to New York City FC fans for the first time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: We are also incredibly excited that Gotham FC, the reigning National Women's Soccer League champions, are set to begin play at the stadium in 2028.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: The creation of a 25,000-seat soccer-specific stadium represents a significant investment in the future of professional soccer in our city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: The stadium's development is part of the broader transformation of Willis Point into a vibrant, mixed-use neighborhood, and the club believes that ensuring that the neighborhood is served by a robust, accessible, and diverse transportation network is essential to the community's long-term success.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: Intro 846 represents an opportunity to further strengthen that network.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: For New York City FC, expanded ferry service would give our

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: Supporters, another convenient way to get to Etihad Park on match days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: Providing an alternative to driving could also help reduce traffic congestion in the surrounding area, benefiting area residents while making it easier for fans to get to and from matches.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: Beyond the benefits to New York City FC, regular ferry service to Willits Point would improve transportation options for Queens residents and support the area's continued growth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: With new housing and businesses coming to Willits Point, additional transit options will be important to making the neighborhood more accessible to residents and visitors alike.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: New York City FC looks forward to working with the council, the mayor and his team, and our community partners to advance this legislation and support the continued growth of Willits Point and the beautiful game in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Neve Wallace
utterances.text: Thank you for your consideration.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: The City Island Civic Association vice president says infrastructure and parking are inadequate; he recommends Orchard Beach with 5,000 parking spaces and transit access, which would serve the broader Northeast Bronx.
chapters.title: Ricardo Garcia opposes City Island ferry, suggests Orchard Beach

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Ricardo Garcia, followed by Stephen DiFiori.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Maloney, Chairs of Bru, Council Members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: I'd like to take the opportunity to discuss this intro 1032.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: I am a member of the City Island Civic Association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: I'm the Vice President.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: And as such, I wanted to note that we are not opposed

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: to a ferry coming to the Northeast Bronx were opposed to it being on City Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: Currently, the infrastructure, the parking congestion, the parking availability and the congestion would not be alleviated and it just doesn't have the infrastructure for it to properly house

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: a waterfront ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: There were multiple studies that were done, and this had already notated that, plus the low ridership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: What we recommend and what we asked was that it be re-adopted for Orchard Beach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: And the reason why is there was a capital investment project that was recently completed that revitalized Orchard Beach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: In addition to that, there's a parking lot within Orchard Beach that can house approximately 5,000 vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: Plus, there's public transportation access to Orchard Beach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: Which were the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: alleviate some of the flow into City Island and the traffic issues that may arise as a ferry being placed on City Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: So Orchard Beach by far is the most logical and comprehensive place to locate this potential ferry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: Secondly, it would consider if the study, if it's placed at Orchard Beach, it would

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: provide easier access for commuters from Country Club, City Island, Baychester, Echester, Co-op City, Pelham Bay, Pelham Parkway, and also potential clients from Pelham Manor, New Rochelle, and White Plains,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: which would increase ridership and provide the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: The ridership needed to be able to have an ROI on this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: So my recommendation and my ask is that it be reconsidered and repurposed for Orchard Beach instead of City Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: That would make more logical sense.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ricardo Garcia
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: A Pelham Bay resident and union member says a ferry would cut commutes, revitalize businesses, and reduce car traffic; the Bronx has the least developed ferry routes; he urges passage of Intro 1032.
chapters.title: Stephen DeFiori supports City Island ferry for commute and economy

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: And the last testimony is from Stephen DiFiori.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie McCormick
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: Thank you for this very informative meeting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: My name is Stephen DeFiori.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: I am a city worker, a proud union member from DC 37, local 1113, and lifelong resident of Palin Bay, which neighbors City Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: I'm one of the 350 people who have sent a letter to the council in support of Intro 1032 to begin the process of putting a ferry on City Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: There are many reasons why I support this bill, and I will illuminate three.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: Firstly, a ferry on City Island will cut commute times for its residents working in other boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: Currently, residents of the island have to either drive or take a bus to Palin Bay Station, where they transfer to any number of bus lines or the 6 train, and may still require another transfer after that, depending on where in the city they work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: Secondly, City Island is in dire need of economic revitalization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: Unfortunately, many businesses that once adorned City Island Avenue have shut their doors due to a lack of customer traffic, resulting in lower revenues for their businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: However, a ferry stop would make a usually inaccessible part of the city open to many more people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: City Island is a beautiful community with arguably some of the best views in the city and unarguably the best seafood restaurants in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: A ferry stop here would be a huge economic benefit to these great businesses, reduce car traffic on the island, and allow more New Yorkers to experience this legendary part of the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: Lastly, the Bronx has the least developed ferry routes in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: For too long, residents of the Bronx have been an afterthought in a variety of services and resources.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: We deserve it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: So, so much better.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: That is why I hope you will pass Intro 1032 to begin this process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stephen DeFiori
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Maloney thanks Council Member Farias and all testifiers, then adjourns the hearing.
chapters.title: Chair Maloney concludes hearing

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: I believe that concludes our testimony.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: I want to thank Councilmember Farias for being here till the end of the hearing and everyone for testifying today.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: And with that, we conclude the hearing.

summary: Joint hearing of the Committees on Economic Development and Transportation and Infrastructure on NYC waterways, focusing on NYC Ferry, seaplanes, party boats, and four ferry expansion bills.
EDC and DOT testified on ferry finances, route redesign, contract, seaplane oversight, and public piers; council members questioned costs, equity, accessibility, and safety.
Public testimony included City Island ferry supporters and opponents, Waterside seaplane noise complaints, disability advocates, and Willets Point, Canarsie, and Inwood ferry advocates.
title: Committee on Economic Development
topic: Oversight - Transit on NYC’s Waterways: Seaplanes, Party Boats, and the Future of Ferry Service
